name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.exists_maximalAbelian_containing_isSelfAdjoint
title: A maximal abelian subalgebra containing a self-adjoint element

content.display_title: A maximal abelian subalgebra containing a self-adjoint element
content.one_sentence_role: Starts with the algebra generated by the given element and extends it by inclusion-maximality.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $x\in A$ satisfy $x^*=x$. There is a unital $*$-subalgebra $D\subseteq A$ which contains $x$ and is maximal among commutative unital $*$-subalgebras.
content.assumptions: There is no assumption that $x\ne0$, that $A$ is nonzero or separable, or that a representation has been chosen.
content.conclusion: The same $D$ is commutative, inclusion-maximal among commutative unital $*$-subalgebras, and contains the specified $x$.
content.proof_summary: Self-adjointness supplies normality; apply the normal-element containment theorem, whose maximality comes from Zorn’s lemma.
proof_steps: Self-adjointness gives $xx^*=x^*x$, so $x$ is normal. The normal-element theorem [Maximal abelian containment for a normal element](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/MaximalAbelianContaining.lean#L17-L55) therefore applies to this $x$. Its starting subalgebra is the closed unital $*$-subalgebra $E=C^*(1,x)$; normality makes $E$ commutative and $x\in E$.

Consider all commutative unital $*$-subalgebras containing $E$, ordered by inclusion. This set is nonempty because it contains $E$. A nonempty chain has the union as its algebraic star-subalgebra upper bound: finitely many elements needed in an algebra operation lie together in one chain member, and any two elements commute there. This is the directed supremum used in the source. An empty chain is bounded by $E$. Zorn’s lemma gives a maximal such $D$.

If a commutative unital $*$-subalgebra $F$ contains $D$, then it also contains $E$, so the maximality just obtained forces $F\subseteq D$. Thus $D$ is maximal abelian in the full sense, and $x\in E\subseteq D$. The separate result [Maximal abelianness implies norm closedness](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/MaximalAbelian.lean#L67-L80) also gives norm closedness: $\overline D$ is a commutative $*$-subalgebra containing $D$, so maximality forces $\overline D=D$.
